A full-day excursion with an English-speaking guide and private transfer to the charming town of Cafayate, situated in the Calchaquí Valley among picturesque rivers and vineyards.

## Journey Through the Valley

First comes a four-hour journey through the valley. One of its principal attractions is Quebrada de las Conchas, a gorge along the Cafayate River as it flows down from the mountains into the valley. Sparse greenery lines the almost dry riverbed, but the real spectacle is the remarkable red and other colored rocks all around, sculpted into unusual shapes: an amphitheater, an obelisk, Indigenous people with llamas, a frog, a monk — or whatever else your imagination suggests.

The almost magical beauty of the region can be felt everywhere: in the power of the Río Colorado waterfalls, the dazzling white sands of the dunes, and Cafayate's majestic and mysterious landscapes. The place's reputed mystical qualities attracted Inca magicians, while its beauty left Spanish conquistadors, explorers and travelers breathless.

## The Valley and Town of Cafayate

The Cafayate Valley is known for its Torrontés wine, whose refined aroma brings together notes of muscat and jasmine. Arrival in the town of Cafayate, described as founded by the Incas and conquered by the Spanish in 1535. This attractive town lies in the Calchaquí Valley, surrounded by picturesque rivers and vineyards. Its main buildings, including the church, town hall and Archaeological Museum, combine colonial architecture with Baroque elements.

The excursion includes a visit to the main square and a well-known wine cellar to taste excellent varieties of Argentine wine. Return to Salta in the evening.

## Stone Figures and Mortiño Waterfall

Alto de los Ídolos is located near Isnos in the department of Huila and forms part of the archaeological heritage of the San Agustín region. Stone statues, sarcophagi and burial structures from ancient societies of the upper Magdalena River valley have survived here. The figures have large faces and unusual details: they reward a closer look as you imagine what their creators intended these images to mean.

The second part of the excursion's name refers to Mortiño Waterfall, also known as Salto del Mortiño. It plunges into a deep green canyon near the road between San Agustín and Isnos. After the stone sculptures, this landscape offers a very different impression: moving water, lush vegetation and the depth of the gorge opening up below.

This excursion suits travelers who want to combine archaeology with Colombia's natural scenery. Bring comfortable shoes with good grip and light protection against rain. The exact viewing areas and any additional activities are selected as part of the agreed itinerary.

## Exotic Bird Park

The Bird Park is located near Iguaçu National Park. This exotic bird park covers four hectares of pristine subtropical forest. Here you can see, and even feed, more than 500 species of exotic birds from various continents in a natural habitat.

The reserve is also home to crocodiles, monkeys and other animals. You will enter enormous aviaries where beautiful birds of extraordinary colors fly or roam freely amid the tropical forest.

## Santos and Guarujá in One Day

Santos and Guarujá reveal Brazil's coastal side close to the vast city of São Paulo. In Santos, maritime life is intertwined with the history of its port and trade. Buildings that recall the city's development survive in the old center, while a strip of gardens runs alongside the beaches. It is a pleasant landscape to explore from both the city streets and the shore.

Guarujá is known for beaches and bays separated by green headlands. Here, urban development lies close to the sea, and each bend in the shoreline brings a different view of the water. Together, these two cities offer contrasting experiences of the coast: a historic port and resort landscapes.

This full-day excursion takes place with a Russian-speaking guide. It is ideal for travelers who want a break from the metropolis to enjoy the sea air and get to know the coastal towns. The exact stops, time at the beaches and additional visits are determined by the agreed itinerary.

Tigre lies approximately 40 km from Buenos Aires among the islands and waterways of the Río de la Plata delta.

On a sightseeing boat trip, you will see mansions, green parks, restaurants and cafés along the water.

The itinerary also includes the San Isidro district, the presidential residence at Quinta de Olivos and the building of the Rowing Club, constructed in the 19th century.
